name: Goldenes Dachl
kurzbeschreibung: Innsbruck's landmark: the late-Gothic oriel of Emperor Maximilian I with 2,657 gilded copper shingles.
beschreibung:
The Golden Roof (Goldenes Dachl) is the landmark of Innsbruck and is located on Herzog-Friedrich-Straße in the Old Town. Emperor Maximilian I had the late-Gothic oriel built between 1497 and 1500 on the south front of the government building known as „Neuhof“. The master builder and creator of the reliefs is considered to be Nikolaus Türing the Elder, while the fresco decoration is attributed to the court painter Jörg Kölderer.

The roof is covered with 2,657 fire-gilded copper shingles. Originally the oriel served the emperor as a box at festivities and tournaments. Today the Museum Goldenes Dachl tells the story of the building and of Maximilian I; six restored original reliefs can be seen there. From the oriel there is a view over Innsbruck's Old Town.
